listing.name: Elf Bowling / Elf Bowling Recomp
listing.summary: Bowl with your own copy of the original 1999 Elf Bowling executable.

steps.title: Select the unmodified original
steps.instruction: Use your own 1,130,496-byte Elf Bowling.exe from the 1999 release, and keep your original separately. On first start the player asks you to choose it, checks its SHA-256 and keeps a copy in its app profile.

steps.title: Choose the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Linux x64 with glibc 2.38 or later, use the v1.1 AppImage. Set PORT_FULLSCREEN=0 to start in a window. For Windows x64, choose v1.0 in the release picker, extract the full ZIP, and run elfbowl.exe with its bundled libraries. In a copy you manage yourself, you can also put the original next to the player or point ELFBOWL_EXE to it.

steps.title: Use the separate Android or Mac setup
steps.instruction: The v1.0 release has an Android APK for ARM64 and x64. It uses Android’s file picker for the original. The upstream Mac instructions build from source with SDL2 and SDL2_ttf. The publisher supplies no Mac or Linux ARM64 package.

steps.title: Keep the app profile
steps.instruction: Preserve the NStorm/Elf Bowling profile before replacing the upstream player. It is normally under XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, and under %APPDATA% on Windows. Android keeps its app files separately. Keep any optional locally generated artwork with the copy that uses it.

warnings: The project has not published a license for its engine source. The original game is supplied separately.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, the player asks you to choose your own 1,130,496-byte Elf Bowling.exe from the 1999 release. It checks the file's SHA-256, copies it into its NStorm\Elf Bowling profile under %APPDATA% and uses that copy from then on; keep your original separately and do not put it in Portcove's install folder, where an extra program holds launch and updates. Cancelling the picker shows a message and closes the game. The package is the player with SDL2 libraries; the original game is never included. The project has not published a license for its engine source. The player works from its profile folder, so the copied original and everything the game writes stay in %APPDATA%\NStorm\Elf Bowling, outside the managed copy. Portcove neither backs them up nor removes them, and rollback does not rewind them. Portcove replaces the player; you own the original and the profile.
